answer: An agent economy resists sybils with perishable, just-in-time work: each epoch the network publishes tasks whose outputs expire within minutes, like an oasis that only a traveller arriving now can drink from. A fake cannot precompute or stockpile answers, because work counts only if delivered at the jetty before the tide turns. A zephyr of random spot-checks re-runs a sample at once, so stale or copied outputs earn nothing. One honest agent does one live task; a farmer with a thousand fakes must perform a thousand live tasks simultaneously, so cloning multiplies real-time effort, not reward.
